headline: High: Semantic Kernel’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify Botpress outputs into data leakage and cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is moderate via shared tool/content channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress can emit chatbot content, and Semantic Kernel can consume files, MCP tools, and plugin outputs; that creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Botpress output is fed into SK without sanitization. No direct shared channel is documented, so I cannot justify high. The pairwise pathway is inferred from both profiles’ I/O surfaces.
conditions: IF Botpress output is passed into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF an MCP server or file bridge relays Botpress text into SK tool calls, attacker instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Add a strict prompt/content delimiter before SK ingests Botpress text.
Strip tool directives from Botpress outputs before forwarding.
Require human review for any Botpress-generated action request.
Disable MCP/file bridges between the two agents unless needed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and allowlist-based parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel explicitly reads/writes application-defined files and sends context to external model providers; Botpress is a chatbot agent that may surface user content. If they share a workspace or Botpress outputs sensitive text into SK, SK can exfiltrate it through broad egress. The leakage path is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Botpress and Semantic Kernel share files or prompts containing sensitive data, SK can transmit that data to model providers.
IF Botpress stores user content in a workspace readable by SK, SK may leak it via API calls.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Keep secrets out of shared files and prompts.
Turn off SK plugins that forward raw file contents.
Use per-agent credentials with least privilege.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any outbound API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Semantic Kernel can write files and use plugins/MCP in a per-kernel shared-state model. Even though Botpress lacks filesystem write and SK cannot modify git state, overlapping mutable surfaces still exist through files and plugins, so conflict is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents target the same application-defined directory, writes can overwrite each other.
IF Botpress package installation changes runtime dependencies used by SK, execution can diverge.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Freeze dependencies before running both agents.
Avoid shared mutable plugin state.
Serialize writes to any common workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is designed for function-calling against plugins and can act on application context; if it treats Botpress output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream API actions. Botpress is a customer-support agent, so its generated content may be operationally acted on. The default path is dangerous because verification is not shown.
conditions: IF Botpress-generated text is used as SK tool input without verification, SK may execute incorrect actions.
IF SK plugins have side effects, a mistaken Botpress recommendation can trigger irreversible external changes.
mitigations: Require a verification step before any SK tool call.
Restrict SK plugins to read-only actions.
Log and review Botpress-to-SK handoffs.
Add schema validation for Botpress outputs.
requires-engineering: implement approval gates for side-effecting plugins.

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no residency or retention details here, while Semantic Kernel explicitly handles model provider API keys and plugin credentials and can send context to Azure/OpenAI/Hugging Face/MCP servers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for regulated data classes, but the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdictional violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Semantic Kernel plugins or model providers, retention/residency obligations may be violated.
IF Botpress collects customer-support data and SK forwards it to third-party APIs, compliance controls must be aligned.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent.
Block regulated data from SK plugins by policy.
Review provider DPAs and residency settings.
Minimize logging of prompts and outputs.
requires-engineering: add compliance-aware routing and retention enforcement.
